_help: Your relay defaults, used by the 'relay' command, the Herdr 'Start AI relay' dialog and agents' 'relay' setup. Anything you choose when starting a relay overrides these. team: which team runs by default. teams: roles in order; each role has a job, a default agent (claude | codex | antigravity) and effort (low | medium | high | xhigh | max | default); once = first pass only; judge = approves or asks for changes (default: the last role). strengths: what each agent is good at; queue mode picks each task's agents from these. effort: 'recommended' (each role's own effort), 'none' (agent defaults) or 'role=level,...'. model: 'default' or 'role=name,...'. The executor always runs at high effort or above. codexApproveForMe: Codex stages start with --approve-for-me (no repeated git approval prompts). codexWindowsSandbox: the Windows sandbox Codex stages run in (-c windows.sandbox=<value>; default 'mxc'; 'none' = leave it to your Codex config). overnight: settings for unattended -Overnight runs (see its own _help). To add a team, copy _exampleTeam into teams under a name of your own (e.g. "docs").

coding.job: Write or update the task file .ai/tasks/T-xxx.md (goal, approach, files, acceptance criteria). No production code.
Implement the task file. Do not change its acceptance criteria; note any deviation in its Notes.
Test against the acceptance criteria in the task file, write tests, fill in its Test report. Report bugs instead of fixing production code.
Review the changes against the task file and .ai/DECISIONS.md and write your findings in its Review.

_exampleTeam.job: Outline the document in .ai/tasks/T-xxx.md: sections, audience, sources. No final text.
Write the document from the outline. Keep to the outline's sections.
Check the text for accuracy and clarity; list what must change in the task file's Review.

strengths.claude: planning, architecture, code review, tricky logic, writing
strengths.codex: static assets (images, icons, illustrations via image generation), scripts, tests
strengths.antigravity: app code, UI and full features, refactors

overnight._help: Used with -Overnight (or the Overnight box in the dialog). skipPermissions: start every agent with its permission checks off (claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, agy --dangerously-skip-permissions). until: no new task starts after this time ('08:00'), or 'done' = no time limit. maxCycles: plan-and-run cycles in queue mode, 0 = no limit. Whichever limit comes first ends the night; it also ends when nothing worthwhile is left. stallMinutes: no progress for this long = nudge, then skip. maxStageMinutes: a stage is interrupted after this long.

fallback._help: What the relay does when an agent's plan quota runs out (D-027). enabled: false = only wait, as before. waitMinutes: a limit that resets within this many minutes is waited out; a longer one makes the relay switch. models: each agent's model chain, best first (short names: antigravity hydrogen | flash | opus | sonnet | gpt-oss, claude fable | opus | sonnet | haiku, codex sol | astra | terra | luna). Antigravity's Gemini models (hydrogen, flash) share one quota, so its chain moves to Antigravity's Claude models and GPT-OSS. A model out of quota is switched inside the running session (no work lost); when an agent has no model left, another agent takes over the stage (agents: who to try, in order). basicModels may only test, never plan, build or review. lowerEffortAtPercent: when Claude's or Codex's plan use is at least this high, the roles in lowerEffortRoles start one effort step lower (tester down to low; reviewer only in fix rounds, down to medium). The executor and planner never lose effort. Quota planner (D-029): maxWaitMinutes = no stage waits longer for a quota, then it switches; claudeReservePercent = above this share of Claude's 5-hour limit new stages go to other agents, so your own Claude chats keep working (the judge may use Claude up to judgeClaudePercent); predict = before a stage, skip an agent whose plan probably can't finish it (learned from usage/model-stats.jsonl) when its reset is more than maxWaitMinutes away; allOut 'free-models' = when every agent and the OpenRouter budget are out, go on with free OpenRouter models (any role, flagged), 'wait' = wait for the first reset.

opencode._help: OpenCode on OpenRouter models (D-028). models: per role, best first; the relay takes the first one OpenRouter lists right now with tool calling, that has quota left and that the budget allows, and uses its free ':free' variant when one is listed and the project may use free models. freeModelProjects: project folder names that may use free models (their providers may keep prompts), or 'all'. budgetStopPercent: paid models stop when the key has used this much of its OpenRouter limit; free ones go on. budgetPace: 'weekly' = paid models may only use the share of the monthly limit for the weeks passed so far (unused weeks carry over), 'daily' the same per day, 'none' = only the limit. Every stage of every agent is recorded in usage/model-stats.jsonl; tools/model-report.ps1 turns it into the model report and suggestions (weekly task 'AI relay model report').

scout._help: The model scout (tools/model-scout.mjs, D-032) grades OpenRouter models for OpenCode from credible sources (OpenRouter's data incl. Artificial Analysis and Vals indexes, Terminal-Bench; SWE-bench and Aider only while recent) plus our own benchmark (tools/model-bench.ps1) and real relay results. autoPromoteRoles: roles whose list it may change by itself, only on measured evidence; other roles get a proposal you accept in the panel. minMargin: points a challenger must lead by. goodEnough: a measured first choice at or above this gets no paid challengers. trialEvery: 1 in this many tester stages tries the scout's trial model (free models, projects that allow them). paidBenchCapUsd: most a paid benchmark stage may cost (estimated); maxPaidBenchPerWeek: paid models measured a week. sourceMaxAgeDays: older sources are skipped. maxOutPricePerM / minContext: what counts as a candidate.
